This diff adds a new opt-in --phylogenetics stage: a CDS-nucleotide FASTA parser, three-way candidate selection (human-affecting-or-likely / divergence-candidate / complete-triplet isolates, requiring CDS for all of S/M/L and excluding lab/vaccine strains and unclassified species), MAFFT alignment + IQ-TREE ML phylogenetics per species/segment via subprocess, tree-based divergence diagnostics, bootstrap-gated reassortment call classification, and Robinson-Foulds tree comparison via dendropy. It has already been run end-to-end successfully on real data (14 species, ~1500 candidate isolates, no failures) and just had a /simplify pass applied (deduped a FASTA-parsing loop into a shared generator, deduped a rank-normalization statistics block into shared helpers, removed redundant module-reference parameters from _analyze_species, fixed an O(n^2) clade-lookup in _patristic_distance_matrix). Focus this review on CORRECTNESS bugs only (crashes, wrong results, data corruption, unsafe subprocess/file handling, edge cases in the candidate-selection and tree-parsing logic) -- not simplification/style, that pass already happened. Default (no --phylogenetics flag) pipeline behavior must remain byte-for-byte unaffected; flag anything that risks that.

result.summary: test (4 additional verified findings appended unmerged.)

findings.summary: The opt-in --phylogenetics block was inserted before the 'Writing outputs' section instead of after it, so any exception/SystemExit raised while running the phylogenetics stage (missing mafft/iqtree binaries, missing biopython/dendropy, or any bug in parse_cds_fasta/collect_phylo_candidates/run_phylogenetics_stage) aborts run_pipeline before a single one of the standard parquet/json outputs (ortho_accession_table, ortho_species_table, ortho_isolate_table, ortho_risk_table, ortho_ml_*, ortho_qc_report, ortho_summary.json, etc.) is written.
findings.failure_scenario: A user runs `python all_hanta.py --phylogenetics` in an environment where mafft/iqtree aren't on PATH (or biopython/dendropy aren't installed) -- exactly the setup mistake the README explicitly warns about ('don't just prepend that env's bin/ to PATH'). resolve_binary()/the ImportError check in run_phylogenetics_stage raises SystemExit, which propagates uncaught out of run_pipeline and main(). Because 'logging.info("Writing outputs")' and every safe_write_parquet/safe_write_json call for the core (non-phylogenetics) tables now sit textually after the `if args.phylogenetics:` block, none of them execute: the entire run produces zero output tables (not even ortho_summary.json), even though this feature is documented and designed to be strictly additive/opt-in and the core pipeline is supposed to be unaffected by it. The user loses the whole run over an unrelated, easily-fixed environment issue instead of just missing ortho_reassortment_table.parquet.

findings.summary: The per-species try/except in _analyze_species only wraps run_mafft/run_iqtree, not Phylo.read, the patristic-distance/RF computation, or bootstrap-support lookup, so it only partially re-establishes the 'never aborts the run' invariant it claims (and that transform_one_record's whole-body try/except actually delivers) for a phylogenetics-stage isolate.
findings.failure_scenario: For a species whose IQ-TREE tree is missing a tip that write_segment_fasta wrote (e.g. IQ-TREE silently dropped a duplicate/near-identical sequence during ModelFinder, a known IQ-TREE behavior with `--seqtype DNA` on near-identical CDS), _patristic_distance_matrix's `clades[labels[i]]` lookup (line ~2364, called via tree_divergence_for_species at line 2507) raises KeyError outside the try/except. Because run_phylogenetics_stage (line 2555) and its caller in run_pipeline (line 3294) have no surrounding try/except either, the KeyError propagates uncaught and crashes the whole pipeline run -- not just marking that species 'failed' as documented in the docstring/README, but losing the run entirely, including the ortho_accession_table/species/isolate/ML parquet writes that come after this block (lines 3301+).

findings.summary: _analyze_species only wraps the MAFFT/IQ-TREE subprocess calls in try/except; the downstream Phylo.read, tree_divergence_for_species, dendropy RF computation, and classify_reassortment_call/bootstrap_support_for_pair calls (lines 2504-2536) run outside any exception handler, and run_pipeline has no try/except around run_phylogenetics_stage either.
findings.failure_scenario: If any post-alignment step raises for a given species -- e.g. bootstrap_support_for_pair's `next(tree.find_clades(name=label_a))` (line ~2416) hitting StopIteration on a tip-label/tree mismatch, Phylo.read failing on an unexpected treefile format, or dendropy's shared TaxonNamespace/encode_bipartitions choking on a degenerate tree -- the exception propagates uncaught through _analyze_species -> run_phylogenetics_stage -> run_pipeline -> main(), which has no top-level try/except. Because run_pipeline (as of this diff) runs the entire `if args.phylogenetics:` block *before* 'Writing outputs' (line ~3290), the crash aborts the whole pipeline and no parquet tables at all are written for that invocation -- not just the reassortment table but ortho_accession_table, ortho_species_table, ortho_isolate_table, ortho_ml_feature_matrix, etc. -- directly contradicting the stated invariant ('a species/segment failure never aborts the run, it just marks that species' isolates failed and moves on') and README's 'Nothing is silently dropped' / 'a species/segment failure never aborts the run' claims for a run enabling --phylogenetics on real-world data with any edge-case tree.

findings.summary: The per-species try/except in _analyze_species only wraps run_mafft/run_iqtree, not the Phylo.read/tree-distance/dendropy-RF/bootstrap-lookup code that follows, and run_pipeline sequences the whole --phylogenetics stage before the 'Writing outputs' block with no enclosing try/except anywhere up to main().
findings.failure_scenario: If IQ-TREE succeeds but the .treefile can't be parsed by Bio.Phylo (unexpected characters, IQ-TREE writing an unrooted trifurcation Newick variant it doesn't like, truncated write on a full disk), or dendropy.Tree.get()/treecompare.symmetric_difference chokes because the three trees' tip sets don't line up exactly, or bootstrap_support_for_pair's `next(tree.find_clades(name=...))` raises StopIteration for a missing tip -- none of that is caught. The exception propagates out of _analyze_species, out of run_phylogenetics_stage, and out of run_pipeline uncaught, crashing the whole program with a traceback. Because this block (all_hanta.py lines ~3290-3298) runs before `logging.info("Writing outputs")` and all the safe_write_parquet calls for ortho_accession_table, ortho_species_table, ortho_isolate_table, ortho_risk_table, the ML tables, etc., a single species hitting this gap means a --phylogenetics run produces ZERO output files at all -- not just a missing/failed reassortment row for that species -- directly contradicting the code's own docstring ('a species/segment failure never aborts the run... the same per-unit error isolation transform_one_record uses') and the README's 'nothing is silently dropped' / byte-for-byte-unaffected-default claims, since the only way to get any output on a --phylogenetics run is for every single one of potentially dozens of species-level tree builds to hit no post-tree-build exception at all.

findings.summary: _phylo_row hardcodes n_taxa_in_tree=0 for 'species_below_min_taxa' rows instead of the species' actual candidate count.
findings.failure_scenario: A user filtering ortho_reassortment_table.parquet on n_taxa_in_species_tree to see how close an excluded species was to the --phylo-min-taxa threshold (e.g. to decide whether to lower it and re-run) sees 0 for every below-threshold species regardless of whether it had 1 candidate or phylo_min_taxa-1 candidates, silently discarding information that group_candidates_by_species already computed (it logs 'only {len(members)} candidate(s), need {min_taxa}' but that count never reaches the per-isolate output row).

refuted.summary: bootstrap_support_for_pair's next(tree.find_clades(name=...)) is unguarded and can raise StopIteration, which likewise escapes past the narrow try/except and aborts the run instead of failing just that species.
